**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid binding duplicate cbufs for unused MRT slots**

When a valid subpass has a hole such as `pColorAttachments[0] = VK_ATTACHMENT_UNUSED` and slot 1 bound, this sets `nr_cbufs` to 2 while leaving `cbufs[0]` NULL. The r300g emitter does not keep that slot empty: `r300_emit_fb_state` calls `r300_get_nonnull_cb()` for each slot, and that helper substitutes another non-NULL cbuf for NULL slots. As a result `COLOROFFSET0` is programmed to the real attachment, so a fragment output at Location 0, which Vulkan should ignore for the unused slot, can overwrite the slot-1 attachment.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Derive per-attachment tile geometry for MRT clears**

When valid MRT framebuffers use attachments with the same render area but different underlying image extents, their r300vk tile splits can differ because images are tiled from each image's full extent. This loop indexes every attachment with the reference attachment's `tile_pass` while `fb.width`/`height` also come from that reference; for example, a 4096-wide cbuf0 and 3000-wide cbuf1 with a 3000-wide framebuffer makes tile pass 1 bind cbuf1's 952-wide tile under cbuf0's 2048-wide tile geometry, so load-op clears or draws can address past the smaller attachment tile.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle legal render passes beyond eight subpasses**

When an application creates a render pass with 9 or more subpasses, this fixed cap makes `vkCreateRenderPass`/`vkCreateRenderPass2` fail with `VK_ERROR_UNKNOWN` even though Vulkan exposes no device limit for subpass count and such a pass may use only simple color/depth attachments. This turns otherwise valid render passes into creation failures; allocate the subpass storage from `subpassCount` or otherwise avoid a hard, unadvertised limit.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Count framebuffer tiles for later subpasses**

For a command buffer where subpass 0 has no tiled color target but a later subpass binds a tiled color attachment, the new `R300VK_CMD_NEXT_SUBPASS` framebuffer is replayed only for the tile passes chosen by `r300vk_cmd_tile_pass_count`, which still scans only `R300VK_CMD_BEGIN_RENDER_PASS` entries. On legal large framebuffers this means the later subpass renders tile 0 and leaves the remaining tiles untouched; include `NEXT_SUBPASS` framebuffer entries in the tile-pass count before replaying them here.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject or bind tiled input attachments**

When a newly accepted later subpass reads an input attachment backed by an image split into r300vk tiles, draw replay still hits `r300vk_bind_input_attachment`'s `img->tile_cols > 1 || img->tile_rows > 1` guard and returns without binding the sampler view or `inv_extent`. Legal large framebuffer attachments then execute `subpassLoad` with no input image bound (or stale state), so either reject these render passes/images up front or bind the matching per-tile view for the current tile pass.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Derive depth-only tile geometry before counting DS tiles**

When a render pass has no color attachments and only a tiled depth/stencil attachment, this now raises `tile_pass_count` above 1, but the replay path still takes the `ref == NULL && tile_pass > 0` skip branch in `r300vk_replay_begin_render_pass` before it reaches the zsbuf binding. I checked that path with `rg --fixed-strings r300vk_begin_rp_ref_image src/amd/r300/vulkan/r300vk`; a depth-only 4096x4096 framebuffer will record tile passes for every DS tile but render/clear only tile 0, so this needs to derive `tile_origin`/extent from `ds_image` when there is no color reference instead of just counting it here.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Check subpass allocation size before multiplying**

Removing the fixed subpass cap makes this allocation size depend directly on the application's `subpassCount`, but the `uint32_t * sizeof` multiplication is unchecked before it is passed to `vk_zalloc2`. With a very large `subpassCount`, this can wrap to a small allocation and the subsequent `for (s < subpassCount)` writes past `rp->subpasses`; guard with `subpass_count > SIZE_MAX / sizeof(*rp->subpasses)` and return OOM/unsupported before allocating.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use the origin-selected depth tile for clears**

When the color reference and depth/stencil attachment have different tile grids, this now binds the DS buffer by pass origin, but `r300vk_replay_clear_attachments` still chooses the DS clear surface with the raw `tile_pass`. For example, with a 2x2 color ref and a 1x2 depth image over a framebuffer clipped to one color column, `tile_pass == 2` binds depth tile 1 here, while the clear path skips because `tile_pass >= r300vk_image_tile_count(ds)`, leaving the bound depth tile uncleared before subsequent draws.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Count only render-area tiles for MRT pass replay**

This uses each attachment's full image tile count when deciding whether the whole command buffer is multi-tile. If slot 0/depth and the render area are single-tile but a later MRT attachment is a larger image whose extra tiles lie outside that render area, `r300vk_cmd_tile_pass_count()` now returns >1; submit then sets `inorder_host = false`, so in-submit host transfers/fills that should feed later draws are deferred to the post-fence pass and the draw can see stale data. The count needs to be based on tiles intersecting the render area, not the attachment's full extent.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use the unclamped render area for tile extents**

For render areas wider or taller than `R300VK_R3XX_MAX_RENDER_DIMENSION`, these new tile extents are computed from the already-clamped framebuffer far corner instead of the recorded render-area far corner. A 4096-wide image split into 2048-pixel tiles therefore replays the second horizontal tile with only `2560 - 2048 == 512` pixels, leaving the rest of the advertised Vulkan 1.0 floor extent untouched even though each individual tile would fit the r300 framebuffer cap.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not reject read-only depth input subpasses**

When a subpass uses the same depth/stencil attachment as an input attachment but the depth/stencil reference is in a read-only layout (for example `VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_DEPTH_STENCIL_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL`, with writes disabled), Vulkan allows the fragment shader to read it as an input attachment without creating a writable feedback loop. Please preserve the DS reference layout/writeability and only reject actual writable feedback.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Treat zeroed non-global index terms as source-free**

For an otherwise supported affine-iota kernel where a local/workgroup term is multiplied by zero, e.g. `out[gid] = gl_GlobalInvocationID.x + gl_LocalInvocationIndex * 0`, the multiply path leaves the zero term's `global_only` as false, and this conjunction carries that false into the final affine state. The coefficients still classify as stride 1 / offset 0, so the raster replay would be correct, but the new `affine_global_invocation_only` gate rejects the detector and the dispatch falls through to the compute no-op; zero-coefficient operands should be treated as source-free before applying this source-identity check.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve real global IDs before source gating**

For real r300vk SPIR-V compute shaders, `r300vk_classify_compute_kernel` translates with fragment `nir_options` and then runs `nir_lower_system_values` (checked `src/amd/r300/vulkan/r300vk/r300vk_pipeline.c:1791-1823`); those fragment options leave `has_cs_global_id` at its default false (checked `src/gallium/drivers/r300/r300_screen.c:173-180`), so NIR lowers `GlobalInvocationID` into `workgroup_id * workgroup_size + local_id` (checked `src/compiler/nir/nir_lower_system_values.c:701-708`). With this new guard, a genuine `out[gid] = gl_GlobalInvocationID.x` shader reaches the detector as non-global workgroup/local sources, fails `affine_global_invocation_only`, and falls through to the unknown-shape no-op path, while the new builder tests bypass that pipeline lowering and miss the regression.

For non-sampler descriptor types, `pImmutableSamplers` is ignored, but this new branch treats any non-null value as a valid `VkSampler` array and copies `descriptorCount` entries. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Only reject sampler sets that are actually used**

When the fragment shader has any texture instruction, this scans every uniform sampler variable and rejects the pipeline if any declared sampler is in set > 0. `vk_spirv_to_nir` does not remove dead `nir_var_uniform` variables here, so a shader that samples a set-0 texture but also contains an unused set-1 sampler declaration now fails pipeline creation even though that descriptor is never dereferenced; the check needs to follow sampler derefs used by texture instructions or run after removing dead uniform variables.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Initialize immutable sampler descriptors on allocation**

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve unsigned non-32-bit constants**

When a non-32-bit literal is used only by unsigned integer ops, this unconditional signed read changes values above the signed range before writing the float constant. **<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Offset instance-rate fetches by firstInstance**

With nonzero `firstInstance`, this new `instance_divisor` path does not advance the buffer to the Vulkan base instance. I checked the r300 HW path via `rg --fixed-strings instance_divisor src/`: `r300_draw_*_instanced` passes `i` starting at 0 (`src/gallium/drivers/r300/r300_render.c:739-750`), and `r300_emit_vbuf` computes the fetch offset as `(instance_id / divisor) * stride` without `info.start_instance` (`src/gallium/drivers/r300/r300_emit.c:1083-1086`). Thus `vkCmdDraw(..., firstInstance = N)` reads instance-rate elements 0.. instead of N..; r300vk needs to bias the vertex buffer offset or otherwise account for `draw_first_inst` when enabling instance-rate attributes.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Skip draws when robust instance count is zero**

When a positive-instance draw is clamped to zero because an instance-rate binding is missing or too small, this still leaves `draw.count` positive and the code later calls `pipe->draw_vbo` under only `draw.count > 0`. I checked the r300 draw dispatch with `rg --fixed-strings instance_count src/gallium/drivers/r300`: in the HW path, `info.instance_count <= 1` takes the non-instanced branch (`src/gallium/drivers/r300/r300_render.c:903-917`), so a robust clamp to 0 emits one draw instead of skipping and can touch the invalid instance-rate buffer. Please return or set `draw.count = 0` whenever `robust_instances == 0`.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve instance-rate attributes for one-instance draws**

For draws with `instanceCount == 1` and `firstInstance == 0`, enabling `instance_divisor` here still does not make the instance-rate binding constant for the draw. I checked the r300 HW draw path with `rg --fixed-strings instance_divisor src/`: `r300_draw_vbo` routes `info.instance_count <= 1` to `r300_draw_arrays/elements(..., -1)` (`src/gallium/drivers/r300/r300_render.c:903-920`), and `r300_emit_vertex_arrays` then takes the non-instanced path that explicitly ignores `instance_divisor` (`src/gallium/drivers/r300/r300_emit.c:1049-1050`). As a result, a single-instance Vulkan draw with an instance-rate attribute advances that attribute per vertex instead of using element 0 for every vertex; r300vk or r300g needs to force the instanced emission path whenever any live vertex element has an instance divisor.

When the store buffer index is derived from `gl_GlobalInvocationID` (for example descriptor-array writes indexed per invocation), this call reuses the offset predicate, which returns true for global-invocation-derived defs. That admits a dynamic SSBO binding even though the replay paths only resolve constant/non-dynamic output bindings and otherwise fall back to binding 0, so such kernels can write the wrong buffer instead of being rejected/no-oped.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Admit amul offsets from explicit I/O lowering**

In the r300vk classify path, real SPIR-V SSBO array writes are first lowered by `nir_lower_explicit_io`; that lowering emits `nir_amul_imm` for dynamic array offsets (`src/compiler/nir/nir_lower_explicit_io.c:1197-1202`), and the classify prep only runs copy-prop/DCE/CSE/constant-folding afterward, not `nir_lower_amul`. When a write or copy spills past the starting binding, Vulkan's consecutive-binding rules skip bindings whose `descriptorCount` is zero and exempt them from descriptor-type matching. This check breaks before looking at `next->count`, so a valid layout such as binding 0 = one UBO, binding 1 = zero samplers, binding 2 = one UBO makes a two-descriptor update from binding 0 stop after the first slot, leaving the later descriptor unchanged.
